emergency.title: Emergency Fund
emergency.definition: An emergency fund is a financial safety net for unexpected expenses like medical bills, car repairs, or job loss. It should cover 3-6 months of essential expenses.
commonErrors: Not starting because the goal seems too big
Keeping it in an account that's too easy to access
whatToLook: Calculate your monthly essential expenses first
Start with a small goal (€1,000) then build up
Keep it in a separate, high-yield savings account
Automate monthly contributions

longterm.title: Long-term Investing
longterm.definition: Long-term investing means holding investments for 5+ years to benefit from compound growth and ride out market volatility. It's the foundation of wealth building.
whatToLook: Focus on low-cost index funds for diversification
Understand your risk tolerance before investing
Rebalance portfolio annually, not more often
Consider tax-advantaged accounts first

passive.title: Passive Income
passive.definition: Passive income is money earned with minimal ongoing effort after initial setup. Examples include dividends, rental income, and interest from bonds.
commonErrors: Expecting passive income without initial work/capital
Chasing high yields without understanding risks
Not accounting for taxes on passive income
whatToLook: Dividend yield vs dividend growth strategies
Sustainability of income sources
Tax implications in your jurisdiction
Reinvestment options for compound growth

speculation.title: Speculation
speculation.definition: Speculation involves higher-risk investments with potential for significant gains or losses. Only use money you can afford to lose completely.
whatToLook: Never invest more than 5-10% of portfolio
Have a clear exit strategy before entering
Understand the underlying asset/technology
Keep emotions separate from decisions

riskLevel.title: Risk Levels
riskLevel.definition: Risk level indicates how much potential volatility and loss an investment or tool carries. Higher risk means higher potential returns but also higher potential losses.
commonErrors: Ignoring risk level when choosing tools
Assuming low risk means no risk
Not matching risk to your timeline
Taking on more risk than you can handle emotionally
whatToLook: Green (Low): Suitable for beginners and essential funds
Yellow (Medium): Requires basic knowledge and monitoring
Red (High): Advanced users only, significant loss potential

diversification.title: Diversification
diversification.definition: Diversification means spreading investments across different asset classes, sectors, and geographies to reduce overall portfolio risk.
whatToLook: Mix of stocks, bonds, and alternatives
Geographic diversification (domestic + international)
Sector diversification within equities
Regular rebalancing to maintain target allocation
